Serilog handles this in two scalar conversion policies. One covers `byte[]` and the other covers `Memory<byte>` and `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`.

- **`byte[]`:** `ByteArrayScalarConversionPolicy.TryConvertToScalar` turns the array into uppercase hex. Once the length is over 1024 (`MaximumByteArrayLength`), it uses only the first 16 bytes and appends `... (N bytes)`.
- **`Memory<byte>` and `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>`:** `ByteMemoryScalarConversionPolicy.TryConvertToScalar` handles both types. It passes them to `ConvertToHexString`, which applies the same 1024 limit. Over it, it keeps `MaxTake` (16) bytes and adds the `... (N bytes)` tail. This policy only compiles when `FEATURE_SPAN` is defined.
